ribbondesc: Advancing the frontiers of computational multiphysics through innovative research and cutting-edge numerical methods.

Energetic Materials & Propulsion.title: Shock Initiation & Detonation of Energetic Materials
Energetic Materials & Propulsion.subtitle: Initiation, Hot-Spot Physics, and Microstructure-aware burn models
Energetic Materials & Propulsion.overview: Multiscale, multiphysics study of energetic materials from atomistic chemistry to continuum-scale initiation and run-to-detonation behavior. We combine DFT, MD, KMC and continuum reactive flow models for predictive capabilities.
currentProjects: Hot-spot formation and growth in heterogeneous energetic materials
Reactive burn models coupled to hydrocodes
Multiscale Framework: DFT → MD → continuum
impact: Mechanistic insight into initiation and sensitivity
Improved constitutive/reaction models for engineering simulations
Data-driven parameter calibration linking experiments and simulation

Energetic Materials & Propulsion.title: Solid Propellant Modelling
Energetic Materials & Propulsion.subtitle: From Packed Microstructure to Burn Rate and Grain Integrity
Energetic Materials & Propulsion.overview: Predictive modelling of composite solid propellants starting from the microstructure: we pack realistic oxidiser particles, resolve the burning surface and the flame above it, and follow heat and stress into the solid to study burn rate, cracks and debonding.
currentProjects: Packing of spherical and faceted crystals to measured loadings
Interface-resolved burning of ammonium perchlorate propellants and burn-rate prediction
Coupled thermal and mechanical response of the burning solid
Grain geometry, burn-back and the effect of cracks and debonds
impact: Burn-rate trends predicted from measured material constants
Microstructures built to a recipe and validated against published packs
A route from CT images of real propellant to simulation
Energetic Materials & Propulsion.imgtitle: Packed propellant microstructures with faceted and spherical particles built with PyAMorph (top), and temperature and stress on a burning surface (bottom)

Energetic Materials & Propulsion.title: Propulsion Flows
Energetic Materials & Propulsion.subtitle: Jet Engines, Scramjets and Detonation Engines
Energetic Materials & Propulsion.overview: Whole-device simulations of air-breathing and detonation-based engines with the in-house solver: rotating machinery inside a real engine geometry, shock trains in supersonic inlets, and detonation waves that travel around an annular chamber.
currentProjects: Complete micro-turbojet with rotating compressor and turbine
Shock trains in scramjet isolators and strut combustors
Rotating detonation engines
impact: Engine geometry taken from drawings to a running simulation without body-fitted meshing
Moving parts and reacting flow handled in one framework
Simulations at tens of millions of cells on GPUs
Energetic Materials & Propulsion.imgtitle: A micro-turbojet with rotating compressor and turbine (top) and a rotating detonation engine (bottom), simulated with the in-house solver

Protective Materials & Structures.title: Impact, Blast & Debris Protection
Protective Materials & Structures.subtitle: Multiscale Mechanics and Materials Design for Protection
Protective Materials & Structures.overview: Design and simulation of materials and structures optimized for impact resistance — from microstructural tailoring to structural-scale response — using coupled multiscale mechanics and dynamic testing calibration.
currentProjects: Hypervelocity debris impact on spacecraft bumper shields
Ballistic response of layered and fibre-composite armour
Blast loading of protective structures
Coupling experiments and simulations for validation
impact: Guides design of lighter, more effective protective systems
Translates microstructural design rules to engineering-scale performance
Supports defense and aerospace material qualification
Protective Materials & Structures.imgtitle: Bullet-on-armour geometry built with PyAMorph (top) and a hypervelocity debris impact on a bumper shield simulated in-house (bottom)

Protective Materials & Structures.title: Bioinspired & Architected Protective Materials
Protective Materials & Structures.subtitle: Origami, Architected Lattices and Nature's Armour
Protective Materials & Structures.overview: Nature folds, layers and grades its structures to absorb energy. We design and simulate protective materials that borrow these ideas — origami cells that fold under load, spinodoid and cuttlebone-like lattices, nacre-like layups and bioinspired fibre armour — under impact and blast.
currentProjects: Origami (Kresling) cells as foldable, energy-absorbing structures under blast
Spinodoid and graded porous architectures as shields against orbital-debris impact
Bioinspired UHMWPE–Kevlar armour
Cuttlebone-like and nacre-like lattices and layups
impact: Lightweight structures that fold and absorb energy by design
Geometry generators for origami and architected materials that feed directly into simulation
Design rules for protective structures in aerospace and defence
Protective Materials & Structures.imgtitle: An origami cell under a blast wave (top) and a spinodoid architecture built with PyAMorph (bottom)

Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.title: Hypersonic & Reentry Aerothermodynamics
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.subtitle: Ablation, Aerothermochemistry, and Plasma–Material Interaction
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.overview: Coupled study of high-enthalpy aerothermodynamics, surface ablation and chemistry, and plasma–material interactions encountered during hypersonic flight and planetary reentry.
currentProjects: Ablation and surface chemistry modelling for TPS materials
Aerothermochemical coupling in boundary layers at high enthalpy
Multiscale methods for gas-surface interaction kinetics
impact: Improves predictive models for thermal protection systems
Informs material selection and design for extreme environments
Enables joint experiments and simulation campaigns with hypersonics groups
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.imgtitle: A crew-module and a scramjet-vehicle geometry built with PyAMorph

Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.title: Thermal Protection System Simulations
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.subtitle: Microstructure-Resolved Response of Porous Heat-Shield Materials
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.overview: Heat shields are porous, fibrous materials whose behaviour is set at the scale of individual fibres. We build fibre-felt microstructures, compute their effective thermal and transport properties, and simulate heat conduction, flow through the pores and material response directly on the resolved geometry.
currentProjects: Effective thermal properties of porous fibrous materials from meso-scale simulations
Synthetic and CT-derived fibre-felt microstructures
Coupled conduction and pore-scale flow in resolved microstructures
Material-response models for ablative heat shields
impact: Material properties computed from the microstructure rather than fitted
A link between micro-CT data and vehicle-scale heat-shield models
Support for reentry and hypersonic vehicle design
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.imgtitle: Fibre-felt microstructures for thermal protection materials built with PyAMorph

Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.title: Inflatable Decelerators & Parachutes
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.subtitle: Flexible Structures that Slow a Vehicle Down
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.overview: Ballutes, tension cones and parachutes are thin fabric structures that deform strongly in the flow they are meant to slow. We simulate them with a thin-shell structural solver coupled two-way to the flow solver.
currentProjects: Tension-cone ballutes in supersonic flow
Inflatable aerodynamic decelerators
Parachute canopies
impact: Fabric structures simulated at their true thickness
Coupled prediction of shape, drag and loads
Support for entry, descent and recovery system design
Hypersonics & Thermal Protection.imgtitle: Inflatable decelerator shapes and a crew module under parachutes, built with PyAMorph

Bioinspired Flight & Fluid–Structure Int.title: Bioinspired Flight & Moving Bodies
Bioinspired Flight & Fluid–Structure Int.subtitle: Flapping, Folding and Rotating Wings in Two-Way Coupled Flow
Bioinspired Flight & Fluid–Structure Int.overview: Insects and birds fly with wings that flap, twist and fold, and the flow and the structure shape each other. We simulate this two-way coupling for bioinspired and engineered flyers, from a folding origami wing to flapping insects and rotors.
currentProjects: Origami wing in a turning stream: tip vortex, wake and snap-through
Flapping-wing and insect flight
Rotors and rotary-wing micro air vehicles
Wing response to gusts
impact: Rigid, articulated and flexible bodies in one framework
Thin wings resolved without body-fitted remeshing
Design ideas for small, agile flying vehicles
Bioinspired Flight & Fluid–Structure Int.imgtitle: Two-way coupled simulation of a bistable origami wing with its tip vortex (top) and an insect geometry built with PyAMorph (bottom)

Solvers & High-Performance Computing.title: YALI: In-House Multiphysics Solver
Solvers & High-Performance Computing.subtitle: Adaptive, GPU-Ready and Built for Shocks, Interfaces and Moving Bodies
Solvers & High-Performance Computing.overview: The group's core solver, written in-house on adaptive mesh refinement. One code handles gases, liquids, elastoplastic solids and reacting materials, coupled across sharp, moving interfaces, from low-speed flow to shocks and detonation.
currentProjects: High-order shock capturing with sharp material interfaces
Adaptive mesh refinement on CPUs and GPUs
Elastoplastic solids, impact and fragmentation
Reacting flow and detonation
Moving and deforming immersed bodies
impact: One framework spanning Mach regimes, materials and phases
Runs on national supercomputers and on GPUs
A common base for every application area of the group
Solvers & High-Performance Computing.imgtitle: Shock interaction simulated with the in-house solver

Solvers & High-Performance Computing.title: Thin-Shell Structural Solver on MFEM
Solvers & High-Performance Computing.subtitle: Membranes, Shells and Creased Sheets
Solvers & High-Performance Computing.overview: A finite-element structural solver built on the MFEM library for thin, flexible structures. It uses nonlinear membrane and thin-shell formulations for large deformations, with crease hinges for folded sheets, and couples two-way to our flow solver so that the fabric, canopy or folded panel moves with the flow around it.
currentProjects: Inflatable decelerators: tension-cone ballutes in supersonic flow
Parachute canopies and their inflation
Origami structures: Kresling cells and folding wings with mountain and valley creases
Two-way coupling of the shell solver with the in-house flow solver
impact: Thin structures simulated at their true thickness, without thickening them to fit the flow grid
One structural solver for fabric decelerators, parachutes and origami
Geometry, creases and meshes generated directly from PyAMorph
Solvers & High-Performance Computing.imgtitle: A tension-cone ballute and a parachute geometry built with PyAMorph (top), and the shell mesh of a Kresling origami cell with its mountain, valley and ring creases (bottom)

Software & AI Tools.title: PyAMorph: Tool for Implicit Geometry Modeling & Morphometric Analysis
Software & AI Tools.subtitle: Massively Parallel SDF Framework on Adaptive Meshes
Software & AI Tools.overview: Signed Distance Functions (SDFs), Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG), and AMReX Adaptive Mesh Refinement for high-fidelity microstructure characterisation.
currentProjects: Implicit geometry modeling via SDFs and CSG operations
Chan-Vese segmentation for image-to-SDF conversion
TPMS metamaterial generation: Gyroid, Schwarz P/D, Neovius, BCC/FCC lattices
Automated morphometry for SDFs
impact: Enables simulation-ready microstructure geometry for solid propellant and metamaterial studies
Unified API composing images, STL meshes, and analytic shapes in a single CSG environment
Automated statistical morphometry over particle ensembles
Scalable to large HPC systems via AMReX domain decomposition without memory bottlenecks
Software & AI Tools.imgtitle: 3D porous microstructure reconstructed via Chan-Vese segmentation on an AMReX MultiFab grid

Software & AI Tools.title: Lumina: An AI-Augmented Multiscale Material Informatics Framework
Software & AI Tools.subtitle: Activate-on-Demand Material Data for Extreme Aero-Chemo-Thermo-Mechanical Regimes
Software & AI Tools.overview: A modular Python-based informatics framework that centralizes fragmented multiscale material data—from atomistic simulation datasets to macro-scale experimental records—within a unified repository utilizing a hierarchical XML schema and a conversational AI assistant.
currentProjects: Hierarchical XML-based schema and runtime material parsing architecture
Three-layer data state management (Original, Override, and Active views) for sandbox experimentation
Digitization of Shock Hugoniot databases (e.g., LANL reports) and multi-scale physics integration (Mie-Grüneisen and JWL Equations of State)
Conversational AI assistant utilizing locally deployed LLMs for natural language data querying
impact: Bridges the gap between granular atomistic data and continuum-scale hydrodynamic solvers through a traceable three-level parametric chain
Empowers formulators and simulation engineers with automated constitutive model validation and visualization (DoE stabilization)
Provides a stateless, header-only C++ execution backend suitable for highly concurrent HPC and parallel engineering environments
Enables completely offline, domain-expert-free database querying via automated natural-language-to-SQL conversions
Software & AI Tools.imgtitle: Lumina materials engine: a JWL equation-of-state curve (top) and a shock Hugoniot fitted against experimental data (bottom)

Software & AI Tools.title: Weaver: Design Automation & Optimisation
Software & AI Tools.subtitle: Surrogate-Based Optimisation for Aerospace Design
Software & AI Tools.overview: A toolkit that automates the loop from a parametric design to its analysis and optimisation, using surrogate models to keep the number of expensive simulations small.
currentProjects: Aircraft and wing–propeller design automation
Surrogate-based optimisation with constraint handling
Optimisation of architected protective materials
impact: Design studies that would otherwise need thousands of simulations
A common optimisation layer for the group's solvers and geometry tools

Software & AI Tools.title: AI & Surrogate Modelling
Software & AI Tools.subtitle: Physics-Aware Learning and AI Assistants for Simulation
Software & AI Tools.overview: Machine learning used alongside simulation: physics-aware neural networks that learn the dynamics of shocked materials and multiphase flows, fast surrogates for design, and language-model agents that set up and run simulation workflows.
currentProjects: Physics-aware recurrent convolutional neural networks (PARC) for shocked energetic materials and multiphase flow
Neural-operator surrogates for aerodynamic prediction
AI agents that automate CFD case setup and post-processing
Language models and retrieval for materials data
impact: Closure models learned from meso-scale simulations
Predictions in milliseconds where a simulation takes hours
Less manual effort in setting up and running simulations
Software & AI Tools.imgtitle: Physics-aware recurrent convolutional neural network (PARC) prediction, from our Science Advances paper
